title: Verse 1
words: aṣṭa mahāprātihārya vaibhavadiṃda aṣṭa guṇaṃgaḷoḷoṃdaṃ sṛṣṭige maṃgaḷa paryāyadinita aṣṭama jinage eraguvenu
restored: aṣṭa mahāprātihārya vaibhavadiṃda aṣṭa guṇaṃgaḷoḷoṃdaṃ sṛṣṭige maṃgaḷa paryāyadinita aṣṭama jinage eraguvenu
translation: Through the splendor of eight great miraculous manifestations, [one] among eight qualities, for creation, auspiciousness [unclear phrase]: I bow to the eighth Jina.

title: Verse 2
words: ṭaṇeya kōlu pustaka piṃcha pātreya avatradā kamaṃḍalada navakāramaṃtra siddhige kāraṇaveṃdu bhuvalayadoḷu pēḷda mahimā
restored: ṭaṇeya kōlu pustaka piṃcha pātreya avatradā kamaṃḍalada navakāramaṃtra siddhige kāraṇaveṃdu bhuvalayadoḷu pēḷda mahimā
translation: The glory told in the Bhūvalaya, saying that the ṭaṇe’s (?) staff, book, feather whisk (?), bowl, unclear item, water pot, and Navakāra mantra are a cause of attainment. The wording does not make clear how all these items relate to one another.

title: Verse 3
words: ṭavaṇeyoḷ akṣaradaṃkava sthāpisida vayavavade mahāvratavu avaravarige takka śaktige varavāda navamaṃgaḷada bhuvalaya
restored: ṭavaṇeyoḷ akṣaradaṃkava sthāpisida vayavavade mahāvratavu avaravarige takka śaktige varavāda navamaṃgaḷada bhuvalaya
translation: Within the unclear ṭavaṇe, the letter’s numerical mark was established; the intervening words are unclear. The line then appears to call the Bhūvalaya of ‘nine’ or ‘new’ auspiciousness a boon suited to each person’s ability.

title: Verse 4
words: vihavāṇi ōṃkārada atiśaya vihanina mahāvīravāṇi eṃdenuva mahimeya maṃgaḷaprābhṛtavenuva mahasidha kāvya bhūvalaya
restored: vihavāṇi ōṃkārada atiśaya vihanina mahāvīravāṇi eṃdenuva mahimeya maṃgaḷaprābhṛtavenuva mahasidha kāvya bhūvalaya
translation: Bhūvalaya, the [ಮಹಸಿಧ?] poem called the auspicious prābhṛta of the glory called Mahāvīra’s speech; [ವಿಹವಾಣಿ?], the excellence of Oṃkāra, [ವಿಹನಿನ?].

title: Verse 5
words: hakau dvisaṃyōgadoḷage ippatteṃṭu prakaṭadoḷ aravattaṃ kūḍe sakalāṃkadoḷ biṭṭa sonneye eṃṭeṃṭu sakalāgama ēḷu bhaṃga
restored: hakau dvisaṃyōgadoḷage ippatteṃṭu prakaṭadoḷ aravattaṃ kūḍe sakalāṃkadoḷ biṭṭa sonneye eṃṭeṃṭu sakalāgama ēḷu bhaṃga
translation: [Unreadable] within a combination of two, twenty-eight; within the display, perhaps sixty also; a zero left among all numbers; eight by eight; all scriptures, seven divisions or modes. The grammatical links between these phrases are unclear.

title: Verse 6
words: kamalagaḷu ēḷu muṃdake pōgutirdāga kramadoḷage eraḍu kālnūru tamalāṃka aidu soneyu āru erḍaydu kamalada gaṃdha bhūvalaya
restored: kamalagaḷu ēḷu muṃdake pōgutirdāga kramadoḷage eraḍu kālnūru tamalāṃka aidu soneyu āru erḍaydu kamalada gaṃdha bhūvalaya
translation: When the seven lotuses were going forward, in order: two, a quarter of a hundred (?), an unclear figure, five (?), zero, six, and an unclear ‘two-five’; the fragrance of the lotus, Bhūvalaya.

title: Verse 7
words: mma hṛdayadoḷā kamalagaḷ calipāga vimalāṃka geluvaṃdavadu samavanu besadoḷu bhāgise soneya kramaviha kāvya bhūvalaya
restored: mma hṛdayadoḷā kamalagaḷ calipāga vimalāṃka geluvaṃdavadu samavanu besadoḷu bhāgise soneya kramaviha kāvya bhūvalaya
translation: Within the heart, as the lotuses move, [something concerning] a pure number is unclear. If the even number is divided by the odd number, [something concerning] the order of zero is unclear in the Bhūvalaya poem.

title: Verse 8
words: siribhūvalaya siddhāṃtada maṃgaḷa pāhuḍhavuṃ aviruddha siddhāṃtavanu mahāvratakeṃdu navapadava aṇuvratakeṃdu saviyāgisi prauḍha mūḍharīrvarige oṃdē navapada bhakti bhuvalaya
restored: siribhūvalaya siddhāṃtada maṃgaḷa pāhuḍhavuṃ aviruddha siddhāṃtavanu mahāvratakeṃdu navapadava aṇuvratakeṃdu saviyāgisi prauḍha mūḍharīrvarige oṃdē navapada bhakti bhuvalaya
translation: The auspicious treatise of the Siribhūvalaya doctrine, too, makes the non-contradictory doctrine pleasing to both the learned and the ignorant, speaking of it as a great vow and of the nine terms, apparently, as a lesser vow; devotion to the nine terms is one and the same—Bhūvalaya. The grammatical connections in the latter part are uncertain.

title: Verse 9
words: viyaliyamalamūḍhadaṃsaṇutaliyā jaya pariṣaha vipateraḍamnaya mārgadiṃda geldavara sadvaṃśada svayaṃsiddha kāvya bhūvalayā
restored: viyaliyamalamūḍhadaṃsaṇutaliyā jaya pariṣaha vipateraḍamnaya mārgadiṃda geldavara sadvaṃśada svayaṃsiddha kāvya bhūvalayā
translation: [Unclear opening] victory, hardship, [unclear phrase]; Bhūvalaya, a self-established poem of the good lineage of those who won by a path.

title: Verse 10
words: yala ela dikkugaḷ hatanu baṭṭeya nalaviniṃ dharisirda muniyu saluva digaṃbaraneṃteṃdu kēḷuva balidanka kāvya bhūvalayā
restored: yala ela dikkugaḷ hatanu baṭṭeya nalaviniṃ dharisirda muniyu saluva digaṃbaraneṃteṃdu kēḷuva balidanka kāvya bhūvalayā

title: Verse 11
translation: O Bhūvalaya poem; the preceding word cannot be read with confidence.

title: Verse 12

translation: O Bhūvalaya that raises victory, if ಗೆಲವೇರಿಸುವ is read that way.

title: Verse 17

title: Verse 18
translation: O Bhūvalaya; the preceding epithet cannot be read securely.

title: Verse 19
words: lāvaṇyadangameyāda gomaṭadēva āvāga tana aṇṇanige īvāga cakrabaṃdhada kaṭinoḷ kaṭidā viśvakāvya bhūvalayā
restored: lāvaṇyadangameyāda gomaṭadēva āvāga tana aṇṇanige īvāga cakrabaṃdhada kaṭinoḷ kaṭidā viśvakāvya bhūvalayā
translation: O Bhūvalaya, world-poem: Gommata Deva is described with an unclear phrase about beauty. The line then says “to his own elder brother then” and “now cut or inscribed within the middle of a wheel pattern”; how these phrases connect is unclear.

title: Verse 20
words: ṇijadahatanu ātmadharmavāgisikoṃḍa bhajakarge śrī viṃdhyagiriya nijatatva ēḷara darśanavanita vijayadhavalada bhūvalayā
restored: ṇijadahatanu ātmadharmavāgisikoṃḍa bhajakarge śrī viṃdhyagiriya nijatatva ēḷara darśanavanita vijayadhavalada bhūvalayā
translation: For devotees who have adopted [unclear opening expression] as soul-dharma, [there is a reference to] the vision [ending unclear] of the seven true principles of venerable Vindhyagiri—Vijayadhavala’s Bhūvalaya.

title: Verse 22
words: ṭkinisiladāhtanu nijdinda tkajnake pēḷda mhimaru aisikaru saṃsāra sāgaradoḷage eṃba coka karmāṭaka valayā
restored: ṭkinisiladāhtanu nijdinda tkajnake pēḷda mhimaru aisikaru saṃsāra sāgaradoḷage eṃba coka karmāṭaka valayā
translation: [Unreadable] … from truth (?) … [unreadable] said … eminent ones (?) … [unreadable] in the ocean of worldly existence, called (?) … [unclear] Karmāṭaka sphere (?). The line cannot be read as a connected sentence.

title: Verse 22
words: ṭidi aṇubhāga baṃdhada pradēśava hoku vidhiyādi hadinālku hoṃdi adaralli nidhiyāgi śivasukhya hoṃdida padave maṃgaḷa karmāṭakau
restored: ṭidi aṇubhāga baṃdhada pradēśava hoku vidhiyādi hadinālku hoṃdi adaralli nidhiyāgi śivasukhya hoṃdida padave maṃgaḷa karmāṭakau
translation: [Opening unclear.] Having attained fourteen [unspecified things] associated with the region or units of bondage and a method of entering [?], and being a treasure therein, the state that attained auspicious happiness is auspicious; the final word is unclear.

title: Verse 23
words: yaśasvati dēviya magaḷāda brāmhige asamāna karmāṭakada risiyu nityavu aravatnālka akṣara hoseda angaya bhūvalayā
restored: yaśasvati dēviya magaḷāda brāmhige asamāna karmāṭakada risiyu nityavu aravatnālka akṣara hoseda angaya bhūvalayā
translation: For Brāhmī, daughter of the goddess Yaśasvatī, the incomparable sage of Karmāṭaka daily wove a Bhūvalaya of sixty-four letters; the word ಅನ್ಗಯ remains unclear.

title: Verse 24
translation: Bhūvalaya, the Om syllable of essence or flavour.

title: Verse 25
translation: Bhūvalaya of fame’s unclear ‘ಎಡಗಯ’.

title: Verse 26
translation: Bhūvalaya of essence or flavour, of three lines or strokes.

title: Verse 27
translation: This line cannot be read reliably.

title: Verse 30
words: karuṇeyaṃ bahiraṃga sāmrājyalakṣmiya aruhanu karmāṭakada siri māta yatnade oṃdariṃ pēḷida aravatnālkaṃka bhūvalaya
restored: karuṇeyaṃ bahiraṃga sāmrājyalakṣmiya aruhanu karmāṭakada siri māta yatnade oṃdariṃ pēḷida aravatnālkaṃka bhūvalaya
translation: He proclaims the compassion of manifest imperial fortune (?); Karmāṭaka’s splendid speech, spoken from one through effort (?), is the Bhūvalaya of sixty-four marks (?).

title: Verse 31
words: jayasiddhiyāda ā oṃdē akṣara brahma nayadoḷaga aravattanālku jainarge smytnadā kaleya atiśaya svayaṃsiddha bhaṃga bhūvalayā
restored: jayasiddhiyāda ā oṃdē akṣara brahma nayadoḷaga aravattanālku jainarge smytnadā kaleya atiśaya svayaṃsiddha bhaṃga bhūvalayā
translation: The victoriously accomplished (?) Bhūvalaya: within the method of that single letter-Brahman, sixty-four, for the Jinas or Jains (?), [unreadable], the wonder of the art, a self-established arrangement (?). The links between these phrases cannot be read securely.

title: Verse 32
words: jāti jāti jarā maraṇavanu guṇākārada ātithya bare bhāgahāra khyātiya bhaṃgadoḷ arivaṃ vikhyāta putavu puṇya bhūvalayā
restored: jāti jāti jarā maraṇavanu guṇākārada ātithya bare bhāgahāra khyātiya bhaṃgadoḷ arivaṃ vikhyāta putavu puṇya bhūvalayā
translation: Birth after birth, old age and death; the hospitality (?) of multiplication, write (?), division; knowledge (?) within the breaking of fame; renowned [unclear word], meritorious Bhūvalaya.

title: Verse 33
words: padapadmadoḷagaṇanka akṣaravijjñāna adara guṇākāra magīladamavamṅvadagi bandā dhyāniya arivige silukiha sadavadhijjñāna bhūvalayā
restored: padapadmadoḷagaṇanka akṣaravijjñāna adara guṇākāra magīladamavamṅvadagi bandā dhyāniya arivige silukiha sadavadhijjñāna bhūvalayā
translation: Knowledge of letters within the word-lotus, its multiplication [unreadable], came (?) into a meditator’s awareness; avadhi-knowledge [uncertain qualification], Bhūvalaya. The full sentence cannot be securely read.

title: Verse 34
words: aṇava padadaṃkadiṃ gaṇisalōmbatamavaranka anulōma bhaṃgada avatārava yatnapūrvaka bhāgisuvanige ēḷu bhūvalaya
restored: aṇava padadaṃkadiṃ gaṇisalōmbatamavaranka anulōma bhaṃgada avatārava yatnapūrvaka bhāgisuvanige ēḷu bhūvalaya
translation: By the number of the ‘aṇava’ word (?), [an unclear counting expression], seven Bhūvalayas for one who carefully divides the manifestation of the forward-order division.

title: Verse 35
words: ṭakada saṃyōgade bhaṃgavāgi hattu sakalāṃka cakrēśvaru akalaṃkavāda hataṃkadō muṃde prakaṭada guṇakāra biṃdu
restored: ṭakada saṃyōgade bhaṃgavāgi hattu sakalāṃka cakrēśvaru akalaṃkavāda hataṃkadō muṃde prakaṭada guṇakāra biṃdu
translation: Through the conjunction of ṭaka, having broken apart, ten; the lord of the wheel of all digits, unstained; [unclear] before; a manifest multiplication point. The grammatical connections between these phrases are uncertain.

title: Verse 36
words: ṭakavanu mahāvīrana aṃtarmuhūrtadiṃ prakaṭise divyavāṇiyali sakalākṣaravaṃ tiḷidirpa gautamana kalanka hanneraḍaṃga
restored: ṭakavanu mahāvīrana aṃtarmuhūrtadiṃ prakaṭise divyavāṇiyali sakalākṣaravaṃ tiḷidirpa gautamana kalanka hanneraḍaṃga
translation: When the ṭaka (?) was revealed within Mahāvīra’s antarmuhūrta, in the divine speech, Gautama—who knew all the letters—[was connected with] the twelve aṅgas; the word between ‘Gautama’ and ‘twelve aṅgas’ is unclear.

title: Verse 37
words: sarvārthasiddhi eṃdenalu akṣarabhaṃga nirvāhadoḷag aṃkabhaṃgaṃ sarvāṃkayōgadoḷ iravattanālkanēl nirvahisalu hattu bhaṃga
restored: sarvārthasiddhi eṃdenalu akṣarabhaṃga nirvāhadoḷag aṃkabhaṃgaṃ sarvāṃkayōgadoḷ iravattanālkanēl nirvahisalu hattu bhaṃga
translation: To call it the accomplishment of all aims: within the carrying out of letter division is number division; within the combination of all numbers, ten divisions are to be carried out in the twenty-fourth (?).

title: Verse 38
words: marmavādāhtaṃ baḷasuva kālade yōgade nirmalaṃ śuddha siddhāṃta dharmava haraḍuva āgina jinapādaśarmara siddha bhūvalayā
restored: marmavādāhtaṃ baḷasuva kālade yōgade nirmalaṃ śuddha siddhāṃta dharmava haraḍuva āgina jinapādaśarmara siddha bhūvalayā
translation: At the time of using [something unclear], through conjunction or practice, the stainless, pure doctrine spreads the dharma; [the relation of] the Bhūvalaya of that time to Jinapādaśarma and ‘established’ is unclear.

title: Verse 39
words: sāgarara dvīpagaḷellava gaṇisuva śrīguru aidavarannu nāgava nākava narakava mōkṣava sādhanavāgisidanu
restored: sāgarara dvīpagaḷellava gaṇisuva śrīguru aidavarannu nāgava nākava narakava mōkṣava sādhanavāgisidanu
translation: The revered teacher, counting all the islands of the oceans, made the five persons (?), the nāga (?), heaven, hell, and liberation into a means. The relation among these objects is unclear.

title: Verse 40
words: rāśiyoḷoṃdaṃ tegeyalā rāśiyu ghāśiyāgadale tuṃbiruva śrīśa anaṃtada padavi hasaṃkhyātada āśeyaṃ anaṃta saṃkhyāta
restored: rāśiyoḷoṃdaṃ tegeyalā rāśiyu ghāśiyāgadale tuṃbiruva śrīśa anaṃtada padavi hasaṃkhyātada āśeyaṃ anaṃta saṃkhyāta
translation: The line may ask about taking one from a heap or quantity, then speaks of something filled, an infinite rank or state, and quantities described as innumerable, infinite, and countable. Its wording does not support a secure complete translation.

title: Verse 41
words: diśeyoḷu baṃda anaṃta saṃkhyātada vaśadoḷa saṃkhyātavadam rasakamalagaḷa ēḷkādirisida divyarasa siddhi jalapadmagaṃdha
restored: diśeyoḷu baṃda anaṃta saṃkhyātada vaśadoḷa saṃkhyātavadam rasakamalagaḷa ēḷkādirisida divyarasa siddhi jalapadmagaṃdha
translation: In the direction came [something] described as endless and countable; within its sway, [unclear words concerning] essence-lotuses, divine essence, attainment, and water-lotus fragrance. The grammatical connection of these phrases cannot be read securely.

title: Verse 42
words: ṭavaṇeyoḷiruva aṃkadoḷu kūḍida ravatu saviyanka eṃṭeṃṭavaroḷa vitiha śrīpadma hadināru svapnada avavayavasthala padmagaṃdha
restored: ṭavaṇeyoḷiruva aṃkadoḷu kūḍida ravatu saviyanka eṃṭeṃṭavaroḷa vitiha śrīpadma hadināru svapnada avavayavasthala padmagaṃdha

title: Verse 43
words: ṭavaṇeyoḷiruva aṃkadoḷu kūḍida eṃṭeṃṭu avanumat punaḥ kūḍidare navava padmavadariṃda baruva aṃka ēḷaṃ savidare beṭṭada padma
restored: ṭavaṇeyoḷiruva aṃkadoḷu kūḍida eṃṭeṃṭu avanumat punaḥ kūḍidare navava padmavadariṃda baruva aṃka ēḷaṃ savidare beṭṭada padma
translation: Within the numeral or mark situated in the unclear ‘ಟವಣೆ’, eight and eight are joined. If [unclear] is joined again, [unclear] lotus; a numeral or mark comes from it. If seven [?] is tasted, [there is] the lotus of the hill.

title: Verse 44
words: samanāda ī mūru padmagaḷa nela mama hṛdayada śuddha rasada āgamakadoḷaṃṭida aṃṭada aṃṭameṃṭaṃ śramavillade sonegedu
restored: samanāda ī mūru padmagaḷa nela mama hṛdayada śuddha rasada āgamakadoḷaṃṭida aṃṭada aṃṭameṃṭaṃ śramavillade sonegedu
translation: These three equal lotuses; the ground of my heart’s pure essence; attached within the āgamaka (?), unattached, [unclear]; without effort, [final action unclear].

title: Verse 45
words: yaśada dhyānāgniṃ puṭaviḍe rasasiddhi vaśavāgudu satya maṇiyu rasamaṇi mōkṣade kāmadavah? eṃba rasidhiynka bhūvalayā
restored: yaśada dhyānāgniṃ puṭaviḍe rasasiddhi vaśavāgudu satya maṇiyu rasamaṇi mōkṣade kāmadavah? eṃba rasidhiynka bhūvalayā
translation: If yaśada is fired in the fire of meditation, rasa attainment comes under control. The true jewel is the rasa jewel; the words after this, concerning liberation and something called rasa attainment, cannot be translated securely.

title: Verse 46
words: lavamātravādarū dōṣagaḷillada navamāṃkada ādi arhaṃta avana eraḍū kālanūrida aṃkada saviye bhāvisise mahāpadmā
restored: lavamātravādarū dōṣagaḷillada navamāṃkada ādi arhaṃta avana eraḍū kālanūrida aṃkada saviye bhāvisise mahāpadmā
translation: O Mahāpadma, even for a moment, contemplate (?) the savor of the mark (?) connected with both feet of the faultless first arhat of the ninth mark or number (?). The wording around the feet and the mark is unclear.

title: Verse 47
words: tarataravāda ela eraḷpādagaḷa nela pādapadmagaḷoḷu baruva atītānāgatadavā oṃdu samayadaṣṭu padadariri vartamānavanu ada aman

translation: Of various kinds … within the lotus feet, coming … past and future … as much as one instant … the present … . The intervening words and their connections cannot be read securely.

title: Verse 48
words: nthaṇathaṇavenuva rasamaṇiyauṣadha gaṇitavaṃ nāgārjunanu kṣaṇadoḷ aridanu guruviṃdal ātanu guṇisutal eṃṭu karmavanu
restored: nthaṇathaṇavenuva rasamaṇiyauṣadha gaṇitavaṃ nāgārjunanu kṣaṇadoḷ aridanu guruviṃdal ātanu guṇisutal eṃṭu karmavanu
translation: Nagarjuna understood in a moment, from the teacher, the reckoning of the rasa-jewel medicine called ‘ನ್ಥಣಥಣ’ (?); he counted the eight karmas.

title: Verse 49
words: sādhisi keḍisuta siddhāṃta mārgada ōdinankākṣaravide mōdada hiṃsā lakṣaṇa dharmadiṃ ādi jinēṃdrara matadiṃ
restored: sādhisi keḍisuta siddhāṃta mārgada ōdinankākṣaravide mōdada hiṃsā lakṣaṇa dharmadiṃ ādi jinēṃdrara matadiṃ
translation: Having accomplished and undoing, [an unclear phrase concerning reading and a letter] of the doctrinal path; through the joyful religion characterized by violence, through the teaching of the first Jinas.

title: Verse 50
words: rāgava gelidavarāga pḷidadvyaṃ nāgasaṃpageya hūvugaḷaṃ sāgarada upamāna guṇitada carite iṃ bhōgava yōgadoḷ kūḍi

title: Verse 51

title: Verse 119
